I’m sorry, but I don’t have the ability to hit the VirusTotal API myself. Below is a quick guide so you can run the request from your own environment: --- ### What you’ll need | Item | How to obtain | |------|---------------| | **API Key** | You already mentioned `my_api`. Keep it secret – never share it publicly. | | **Endpoint URL** | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses//files` where `` is `12.234.56.126`. | | **Parameters** | * `limit`: maximum results per page (`10`).
* `cursor`: value returned by the previous page’s “next” link (`pointer`). | --- ### Example cURL command ```bash curl -X GET \ -H "x-apikey: my_api" \ # <-- replace with your real key "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126/files?limit=10&cursor:pointer" ``` > **Tip:** If you’re working inside a script, store the key in an env variable instead of hard‑coding it: > > ```bash > export VT_API_KEY="your_real_key_here" > ``` > And then reference `${VT_API_KEY}` in your headers. --- ### Using Python (`requests`) – minimal example ```python import os import requests api_key = os.getenv("VT_API_KEY") # set this before running ip_addr = "12.234.56.126" endpoint = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{ip_addr}/files" headers = { "Accept": "application/json", "x-apikey": api_key, } params = {"limit": 10, "cursor": "pointer"} response = requests.get(endpoint, headers=headers, params=params) data = response.json() print(data) # contains file info + next_cursor if more pages exist ``` --- ### Interpreting the Response A successful reply looks like: ```json { "meta": { ... }, "links": { "self": "...", "next": "...", ... }, "data": [ { "id": "", "attributes": { "last_analysis_stats": {...}, "permalink": "...", ... } }, … ] } ``` * `data[]` holds each file object. * Use the `"next"` link (or its embedded cursor) to fetch subsequent batches until you’ve retrieved all desired entries. If there were fewer than ten matching files, the `"next"` field may be omitted—meaning you reached the end of the list. --- #### Quick sanity check 1. Verify your key works against another simple endpoint first, e.g.: ```bash curl -H "x-apikey: my_api" https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/users/me ``` 2. Once confirmed, proceed with the IP‑to‑files request above. That’s everything you need to pull up to 10 files associated with `12.234.56.126`, handling pagination via the supplied cursor. Happy querying!
